DRAFT MINUTES
  ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE
  SEPTEMBER 18, 2018

1. CALL TO ORDER

  CHAIR ZUCKERMAN called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m.

2. ROLL CALL

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT:  Chan-Southwell, Larson, Retz, Stegura,
  Vona (Ex Officio), Chair Zuckerman

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT:  Radocchio, Schachter, Warner

  ALSO PRESENT:  Mayor Pro Tem Mitchell

  STAFF PRESENT:  Assistant to the City Manager Davis,
  Sr. Planner Naughton,
  Administrative Assistant Corea

3. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  APPROVAL OF ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES, JULY 17, 2017

  B.  APPROVAL OF ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING NOTES,
  NOVEMBER 6, 2017

  It was the consensus of the committee to approve Items 3-A and 3-B.

  There being no objection, CHAIR ZUCKERMAN so ordered.

4. AUDIENCE ITEMS

  None

5. DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A.  CLEAN POWER ALLIANCE (CPA) 2019 RATE STRUCTURE

  CHAIR ZUCKERMAN commented that we are one of two cities in southern California who are
  getting power from the CPA; 30 other cities will also participate in 2019. Phase 1 began with
  commercial businesses and there have been billing issues due to the unusual circumstances having
  to do with traffic signal meters. Sr. Planner Naughton further explained the billing issues. CHAIR
  ZUCKERMAN stated that the retention is high for this program and only two businesses have opted
  out.

  1
 CHAIR ZUCKERMAN explained that participants of the CPA program have options to change their
billing, from 36% clean, 50% clean, and 100% clean. The default for commercial accounts is 36%.
CHAIR ZUCKERMAN stated that what has been found is that there is very little savings from 36%
and 50% clean due to solar power available.

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN stated that a list provided shows what other cities have chosen. Five cities,
RHE is one, are at 36%. Five cities are at 100%, fourteen cities are at 50%. Many cities which are
lower income are choosing a higher percentage.

COMMITTEE MEMBER STEGURA commented that the City Council decided on the 36% default
rate for commercial and municipal uses without EAC input. Now that the discussion is regarding
homeowners it is appropriate that the recommendation come from the EAC since it is a citizen
committee and will help homeowners “buy-in” to the decision and aware of the choices and is
pleased that the EAC is participating in rolling this phase to the residents.

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN agreed and stated that the City Council needs advice on this decision and
this is an important element.

Mayor Pro Tem Mitchell stated that there was a deadline approaching when the decision on the
default rate for municipal and commercial uses and was the reason that there was not sufficient
time to bring it back to the EAC. She further stated that at the time, they were not aware of the
minimal difference in cost from 36 and 50 percent.

COMMITTEE MEMBER VONA asked if the municipal and commercial default rate could still be
changed. Sr. Planner Naughton stated that the default rate would be the same for everyone.

COMMITTEE MEMBER VONA commented that she would be in favor of the 50% default rate since
customers can always made changes.

COMMITTEE MEMBER CHAN-SOUTHWELL asked if the different rates will be reflected on the
bill. CHAIR ZUCKERMAN stated that it may just show their current rate. Sr. Planner Naughton
stated that she will need to ask CPA staff. She further explained that customers will get three
notices prior to launch of program and is not sure if the rate options will be explained on these
notices.

Mayor Pro Tem Mitchell suggested communicating this to residents via the City website.

Sr. Planner Naughton stated that SCE is increasing distribution rates. COMMITTEE MEMBER
RETZ asked if the distribution rates to the customer are greater when they choose the “greener”
option. Sr. Planner stated that the distribution will rate will be the same for all customers. Customers
who opt-out will pay the same distribution rate, but will also pay a higher generation rate.

Mayor Pro Tem Mitchell stated that there has been discussion on having quarterly EAC meetings.
COMMITTEE MEMBER STEGURA suggested that the EAC have a web portal in order to share
information amongst committee members.

  2
 Sr. Planner Naughton provided a PowerPoint presentation with background on the Clean Power
Alliance (CPA).

After much discussion, it was the consensus of the committee to recommend to the City Council to
set the default rate tier at 50% for all customers.

There being no objection, CHAIR ZUCKERMAN so ordered.

B.  CITY HALL EV CHARGING STATION STATUS (USAGE)

Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided an update on the status of the EV Charging station,
which has been formally activated as of January 2018. The EAC made the recommendation on
what to charge at the station and there was discussion on how to keep vehicles moving along.
Many cities have a time usage fee, and the committee decided not to do this and rather assess the
concern. Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided information on the stations usage.

COMMITTEE MEMBER STEGURA asked is the report captures after-hours and weekend usage.
Assistant to the City Manager Davis stated that it does, however, the City Manager vehicle is on a
separate account and is not sure if his vehicle is included in the usage reports.

In response to a question by Mayor Pro Tem Mitchell, Assistant to the City Manager Davis stated
that other cities charge about $0.25 per kWh.

In response to a question by CHAIR ZUCKERMAN, Assistant to the City Manager Davis stated that
the EV station is compatible with all vehicle brands.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER RETZ, Assistant to the City Manager Davis
responded that the cost of installing the EV station included undergrounding electricity including
trenching and another station could be added in close proximity to the existing EV station. She also
added, that there is a possibility of adding and EV station at Highridge and Ernie Howlett Park.

Mayor Pro Tem Mitchell suggested that a report on usage be provided to the committee every 6
months.

COMMITTEE MEMBER STEGURA shared that the library would like to install an EV charging
station on the roof and stated that the state has incentives to help with this.

COMMITTEE MEMBER RETZ suggested surveying residents to find out if the community would
like additional EV charging stations.
Assistant to the City Manager Davis highlighted that the report provided that the greenhouse gas
savings equate to planting 41 trees and letting them grow for 10 years.

RECEIVED AND FILED

C.  PARTICIPATION IN THE MOBILE SOURCE AIR POLLUTION REDUCTION REVIEW
COMMITTEE (MSRC) LOCAL PARTNERSHIP PROGRAM

  3
 Assistant to the City Manager Davis stated that this is a funding grant opportunity through the Mobile
Source Air Pollution Reduction Review Committee (MSRC). Staff proposed two EV stations at Ernie
Howlett Park and Highridge Park and a zero emission light duty vehicle and is requesting EAC
members input on the type of vehicle. The City has already applied for this grant and expects to be
made aware if it was awarded after September 20, 2018.

Mayor Pro Tem Mitchell provided a handout by the AQMD which lists the newest EV vehicles
available.

A brief discussion ensued on vehicle options.

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN asked about the locations of the two proposed charging stations. Assistant
to the City Manager Davis stated that the locations could be changed.

A brief discussion ensued on other options for locations of the EV charging stations, with one
suggestion being the library roof.

Assistant to the City Manager Davis stated that if more recommendations are needed from the EAC,
there will be another meeting scheduled.

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN received and filed this item.

D.  ENVIRONMENTAL PROGRAM RECOGNITION

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN asked about the 12 cents per kWh for future incentives. Assistant to the City
Manager Davis stated that incentive will be seen when the city does any future lighting retrofit or
any street light retrofit project.

In response to a question by CHAIR ZUCKERMAN, Assistant to the City Manager Davis stated that
the city is doing well right now since taking advantage of another lighting retrofit in the City at the
end of last year. As a result of that project, the City was awarded Platinum status and will be
recognized next week at the City Council Meeting by the Environmental Service Center. Assistant
to the City Manager Davis thanked the EAC for their recommendations and guidance that
established priorities and goals to get the City to this level. The City was also awarded the Beacon
Award by the Institute of Local Government.

Mayor Pro Tem Mitchell stated there may be a remodel to city hall offices, and there may be energy
saving opportunities that could be reviewed by the EAC.

Assistant to the City Manager Davis stated staff is exploring retrofitting SCE owned street lights.

E.  SUSTAINABILITY ELEMENT UPDATE

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN stated that this is an optional element for the general plan and may be able
to qualify for some funding, but being that there is a substantial budget for the general plan update
and stated that even the grant is not awarded, the sustainability element is important. CHAIR

  4
 ZUCKERMAN encouraged the committee members to attend and participate in the General Plan
Advisory Committee meetings.

COMMITTEE MEMBER STEGURA stated that the General Plan did not include an environmental
or sustainability element, and it is important that it is included now.

Sr. Planner Naughton explained that the goal was to incorporate sustainability throughout the
general plan as opposed to having a stand-alone element. However, the SCAG Sustainability
Grants Program came up and provided an opportunity to add this optional stand-along element.
The goal remains to incorporate sustainability through-out the plan.

Sr. Planner Naughton also noted that SCAG will hire their own consultants to do the work on the
optional sustainability element. There may be a possibility to have the city’s consultants to do the
work.

Sr. Planner Naughton stated that if it is the desire of the Committee and the City Council to make
this a priority then the scope of work with the consultants, Dyett & Bhatia, may need to be revised.

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN suggested that the EAC should still provide input so that it could still be
incorporated throughout the general plan.

COMMITTEE MEMBER RETZ is concerned with the city losing its rural nature and higher density.

Mayor Pro Tem Mitchell stated that the only high density area will be the mixed-use at the top of
the hill in the commercial district.

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN stated that along with this there are concerns with traffic in the commercial
district. The demographics in the city are also changing and younger families may have less affinity
with old traditions.

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN also commented that the state legislature is also requiring cities to have
affordable housing and ADU’s.

Sr. Planner Naughton stated the only element that is not being updated is the Housing Element
since this was already done recently, but encouraged committee members to attend and participate
in GPAC meetings.

Sr. Planner Naughton stated that a housing package was passed last year and ADU’s will not satisfy
the State requirements in the future. Sr. Planner Naughton stated that the city does not have an
inclusionary ordinance and provided a brief explanation of why the city may need to adopt an
inclusionary ordinance.

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN stated that when the city needs to do air quality analysis it must rely on Long
Beach monitoring to measure impacts and this is something that the EAC may want to discuss.

  5
   Mayor Pro Tem Mitchell stated that the AQMD is looking into low cost monitors to determine their
  quality and accuracy. In addition, the EAC may also want to look into sustainability options in the
  city’s commercial district, for example, zero emission vehicles for residents to get around.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER VONA added that in her experience it is best to work with the same
  consultant.

  F.  2019 EARTH DAY

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis stated that in the past the EAC was not involved in coordinating
  this event and staff would like to bring the EAC into planning this event.

6. COMMITTEE ITEMS/FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  None

7. ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR ZUCKERMAN adjourned the meeting at 9:07 p.m. to the next EAC meeting on Tuesday,
  January 15, 2018 at 7:00 p.m.
